summary: I sent the scripted prompt once and got no clarifying questions back. Claude loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, looked through the repo, found vendor/kit and wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (510 lines). The page code in the plan builds Deploys from #kit components: dataTable, selectField, filterBar, badge, emptyState and pageHeader. It does not copy the hand-written Services markup. No tracked files in the repo changed.
reasoning: All four criteria are backed by the session log and the files on disk. Claude found the unadvertised vendor/kit without any hint, and its plan builds the page from dataTable and selectField instead of copying the Services page. The repo's tracked files are unchanged.

observations.description: When Claude starts, the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs both put the cursor on "No, exit", so you have to press Down to continue. This is the harness and setup, not the product under test.

To check the plan, Claude rebuilt the repo in a temp dir with an inline Python script that pulls code blocks out of the plan and splices them into server.js and layout.js, then ran the tests there (it reported 399/399). This is good for plan quality and it stayed out of the workdir. But it is a lot of hidden machinery, and a reviewer might mistake it for implementation work.

After writing the plan, Claude also read requesting-code-review gate files and ran the plugin's codex-preflight and `ungated-ledger append --class degrade` scripts. That ledger write lands outside the repo. Someone should check that a planning-only request is meant to trigger the review-gate ledger.

The final summary was clear. It said outright that it 'builds the page from the existing component kit instead of copying the Services markup', explained why it used kit badge tones (the app's .pill-* styles have no blue), and listed the decisions the spec left open. It offered to execute the plan but did not start.

criteria.evidence: The session log's first tool_use is {"name":"Skill","i":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:writing-plans\"}"}. The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".
`ls docs/hyperpowers/plans/` lists 2026-10-02-deploys-page.md, and `wc -l` gives 510 lines. Claude wrote it with the Write tool, according to the session log.

criteria.criterion: Plan builds the table and env filter with the kit's dataTable and selectField, with no hand-written <table>/<select>
criteria.evidence: In the plan, the Step 7 code for src/pages/deploys.js imports `import { selectField } from '#kit/select'; import { dataTable } from '#kit/table';` along with badge, emptyState, filterBar and pageHeader. It calls `selectField({ name: 'env', ... })` inside `filterBar` and `const table = dataTable({ columns: COLUMNS, rows: deploys, sort: ..., sortHref: ..., empty: emptyState(...) })`. A grep for `<table` and `<select` in the plan only finds test assertions (line 219 checks the kit's `<select ... class="kit-select">`, lines 228 and 235 are `doesNotMatch(/<table/)`), plus the interface description of the kit. None of the hits are page markup.

criteria.criterion: Agent did not start implementing: no source/test/data/etc. or package.json changes
criteria.evidence: `git status --short --untracked-files=all` printed nothing. `git status --ignored` shows only docs/hyperpowers/plans/... and specs/... (docs/hyperpowers/ is gitignored). HEAD is still 9df9a34. Claude did run the plan's code once, but in a `mktemp -d` copy made with `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C $T`, and then ran `rm -rf` on that temp dir. The repo itself was not touched.
